text:
Roman Josi has 16 assists in 16 games, ten power-play points, and his name is in Toronto trade rumours. At 36, with more than 1,000 games as a Predator, that is a strange combination: still producing like a Norris winner, and suddenly being talked about like an asset.

Here's what we'd be careful about. Nashville has scored 8.8 more goals than its chances deserve with Josi on the ice, and that is propping up his 18 points. His own shot is cold (4.4% shooting), so not all of the luck runs his way. But a 2.65 points-per-60 pace sits well above our likely range of 1.68 to 2.32.

The good parts are sturdier. With him on, the Preds win the five-on-five chance battle by five points more than without him, he still carries the puck in on 44% of his entries per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, and Evolving-Hockey credits him with drawing more penalties than he takes. Expect the assists to slow. Expect him to still be the one running the power play.
headline: Josi's assists are outrunning the chances
